sections.overview: The Red Bartsia Bee is a small solitary bee associated with flowering *Odontites*, especially in western Europe.
sections.identification: It is a compact, brown-haired bee with narrow pale bands across the abdomen.
sections.habitat: It favours open, often chalky grassland and other sunny, relatively dry sites where its food plant grows.
sections.diet: Females collect pollen almost exclusively from Red Bartsia (*Odontites vernus*), though the bee may visit other flowers for nectar.
sections.behavior: Adults are most often seen around flowering Red Bartsia in late summer, when bee activity is otherwise waning.
sections.reproduction: Females excavate nest burrows in soil; the species is solitary rather than colony-forming.
sections.ecology: Its close dependence on one pollen plant links its local presence to the availability of flowering Red Bartsia.
sections.conservation: Buglife lists the species as Not Evaluated in its UK profile; that local listing is not a global conservation assessment.
